stories.title: AUSL All-Star Cup — Series 3 Opens Tomorrow
stories.angle: AUSL All-Star Cup Series 3 opens Sunday, August 24 — tomorrow — at Parkway Bank Sports Complex in Rosemont. Teams are set. Captains Kayla Kowalik, Keilani Ricketts, Danieca Coffey, and Devyn Netz have assembled their rosters. With the individual champion crowned after Series 4 on August 30, there are now just 7 days left in the race. Kowalik holds No. 1. Sierra Romero (+42 in Series 2) and Emma Lemley (+26) are chasing. Tonight's angle: preview the Series 3 matchups and the stakes for the individual race.

stories.title: September 1 Countdown — 9 Days
stories.angle: With 9 days until September 1, the focus shifts to the mechanics of how D1 softball coaches prepare their call lists — and what that process reveals about which recruits are genuinely in programs' top tiers. Most coaches have 8–12 players they plan to call in the first hour. Getting on that list requires more than talent; it requires visibility through consistent communication and showcases, a clear desire that programs can sense. Class of 2028 recruits in the next 9 days should confirm their top schools are aware of their interest.

stories.title: USA WNT — 20 Days, Group Oklahoma Preview
stories.angle: Twenty days until USA Softball's WBSC World Cup Group Oklahoma begins at Devon Park, OKC (Sept 12–16). Today's angle is the full group picture: six teams, four days, and the top two advancing to the 2027 Finals in Redcliffe, QLD — the direct Olympic qualifier for LA28. USA (No. 2) is the clear favorite, but Netherlands (No. 6) and Mexico (No. 7) are genuine contenders. A USA team with four OU players on the roster is well suited for the Devon Park environment.

x_posts.text: 20 days until USA Softball opens Group Oklahoma at Devon Park. Six teams. Four days. Top 2 advance to the 2027 Finals in Redcliffe, QLD — the LA28 qualifier. Netherlands (No. 6) and Mexico (No. 7) are the threats. USA is No. 2 and ready. #USASoftball 🇺🇸

stories.title: Oklahoma Softball — First Week of Fall Camp
stories.angle: Oklahoma opens fall camp with a rebuilt roster and something to prove. After the first WCWS miss since 2015, Patty Gasso's program added Macie Harter (.346 BA transfer from MTSU), secured two top-5 2027 commits in Ori Mailo (No. 4, already on campus) and Payton Westra (No. 2), and reloaded after key departures. Fall camp is not just conditioning — it's the first chance for this new group to find out who they are together.

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text: Oklahoma quietly added another major piece this off-season. Sydney Berzon — two-time All-American pitcher from LSU — is now a Sooner. Add that to Macie Harter (.346 BA from MTSU) and a top 2027 class, and Gasso has built something real here. #OUSoftball

stories.title: Texas Softball — Fall Camp Preview, Three-Peat Target
stories.angle: Texas opens fall camp having added Isa Torres (2026 D1Softball National POY from FSU) to a program that already won back-to-back WCWS titles. With Teagan Kavan (2x WCWS MOP) back for her senior year and new additions including catcher Samantha Swan (ASU) and lefty Samantha Lincoln (TTU), the Longhorns arguably enter 2027 as stronger than the team that just won the title. The three-peat has been accomplished only twice in softball history: UCLA (1988–90) and Oklahoma (2021–23).

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text: Before Isa Torres transferred to Texas, she hit .530 at FSU last spring. Set FSU records in BA, runs, slugging, and OBP. Won the D1Softball National POY. Now she lines up next to Teagan Kavan (2x WCWS MOP) in Austin. Three-peat or bust. #HookEm 🤘
